summary: OpenAI describes engineering techniques—model-driven kernel rewrites, load balancing, speculative decoding, caching and an agentic harness redesign—used to cut serving costs and improve efficiency across the GPT-5.6 model family (Sol, Terra, Luna).

mechanisms.reason: The document states concrete, quantified reductions in compute and cost needed per token from kernel, speculative-decoding and load-balancing work.
mechanisms.quote: These efforts, combined with broader kernel advancements from GPT‑5.6 Sol, reduced end-to-end serving costs by 20%.

mechanisms.reason: Speculative decoding improvements to the draft model increased tokens generated per unit of expensive computation.
mechanisms.quote: The resulting improvements increased token-generation efficiency by more than 15%.

mechanisms.reason: The lab frames demand as outpacing capacity and cites large-scale user/business adoption, indicating aggregate inference volume growth.
mechanisms.quote: In a compute-constrained world where model demand is growing faster than capacity, efficiency is core to every system design.

practices.reason: Concrete, reproducible serving techniques (kernel rewrites, speculative decoding, load balancing, KV-cache tuning) with stated cost and throughput gains that an engineering team could apply.
practices.quote: Improvements at every layer compound, with gains coming from optimizations in routing (where requests are sent), scheduling (when requests are sent), kernels (software that runs on GPUs), caching (saved and reused work), and model implementation (the ordering of GPU code).

practices.reason: The described harness patterns (deferred tool discovery, capped tool output, append-only context for prompt-cache preservation) are concrete design choices a team could implement to cut agentic-loop cost.
practices.quote: Tool output is capped at 10,000 tokens by default unless the model requests a different limit.

practices.reason: A third-party benchmark and an internal verification tool are named but described only as the lab's own process, not handed over as a transferable instrument.
practices.quote: We’ve also heavily invested in verification tooling, such as the open-source tool FpSan (Floating-Point Sanitizer), to help validate the correctness of the kernels written by GPT‑5.6 Sol.

practices.reason: The model family is stated to match or exceed competitor/prior-model performance at substantially lower price, directly relevant to cost-sensitive deployment decisions.
practices.quote: Terra performs as well as GPT‑5.5 on intelligence benchmarks at half the price, and Luna is our fastest and most affordable model, priced 80% less than the cost of Sol.

notable_reason: Quantified serving-cost reductions (20% end-to-end, 15%+ token-generation efficiency) are a concrete data point on how efficiency work can offset inference hardware demand growth.
